description: A delay that records into a loop and reads it back at two points, one running forwards through the recording and one running backwards, with the reverse tap feeding back into the loop

params.text: Sets the length of the recording loop, 0.5 to 10 seconds; with a cable in CLOCK the whole number part instead picks a multiple of the clock interval, a sixth of it at 0, once at 5 and six times at 10
Sets how much of the reverse tap is written back into the loop along with the input, from none at 0 to all of it at 1
Sets how far back in the loop the reverse tap reads, from the write point at 0 to a whole loop behind it at 1
Sets how far back in the loop the forward tap reads, from the write point at 0 to a whole loop behind it at 1
Scales the LENGTH input, inverting it below the centre; at full travel one volt adds one second to the loop
Scales the FEEDBACK input, inverting it below the centre; at full travel 10V covers the knob's whole range
Scales the reverse tap's DISTANCE input, inverting it below the centre; at full travel 10V covers the knob's whole range
Scales the forward tap's DISTANCE input, inverting it below the centre; at full travel 10V covers the knob's whole range

inputs.text: The signal recorded into the loop; a polyphonic cable is summed to one channel before it is written
Times the interval between rising edges, reading high at 1.7V, and makes the loop that long; the LENGTH knob then multiplies or divides the interval
Modulates the loop length through the LENGTH trimpot, the total held between 0.5 and 10 seconds
Modulates the feedback amount through the FEEDBACK trimpot, the total held between 0 and 1
Modulates how far back the reverse tap reads, through the trimpot for that tap, the total held between 0 and 1
Modulates how far back the forward tap reads, through the trimpot for that tap, the total held between 0 and 1

outputs.text: The reverse tap, reading backwards through the loop, and the only signal that FEEDBACK writes back in
The forward tap, reading forwards through the loop at the distance set for it, which is an ordinary delay

notes: the module is silent for the first half second after a patch is loaded, while the buffers are cleared
recording runs the whole time and there is nothing to arm, so sound reaches both outputs as soon as INPUT is patched
the reverse tap crosses the write point once per loop, and a 0.2 second crossfade covers the join; one of the lights flashes each time that happens
an unsteady clock drags the read and write points across older material, which clicks; once the delay time is right, unpatch CLOCK and leave LENGTH alone to hold it
turning the reverse tap's DISTANCE while sound is playing adds high-frequency noise, which the maker lists as a known bug

inputs.1:
high above 1.7V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the LENGTH knob sets the loop instead; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.3:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.4:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
